comparisons.peer_topic: Supply Chain Audit and Verification Programs
comparisons.peer_summary: Over the past decade, Intel has engaged with suppliers to verify compliance with the Responsible Business Alliance and Intel Code of Conduct, performing periodic audits and capability-building programs.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and Intel (INTC) disclose specific programs for engaging with suppliers to address sustainability and compliance risks. NVDA aims to engage manufacturing suppliers to adopt science-based targets by 2026, while Intel has engaged with suppliers over the past decade to verify compliance with the Responsible Business Alliance and its Code of Conduct through audits and capability-building. Both disclosures highlight proactive supplier engagement, though NVDA focuses on emissions targets and Intel on conduct compliance and labor risks.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm has established science-based emissions reduction targets approved by the SBTi, including a 50% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2030, a 25% reduction in absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by 2030, and reaching net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by 2040.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and Qualcomm (QCOM) both utilize science-based targets for greenhouse gas emissions reduction. NVDA specifically targets engaging suppliers to adopt these targets to cover 67% of Scope 3 Category 1 emissions by 2026. QCOM discloses that it has established its own company-wide science-based targets (approved by SBTi) for Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions, including a net-zero goal by 2040. Both companies reference SBTi and scope 3 emissions, indicating a shared focus on science-based methodologies for climate action, though NVDA's disclosure centers on supplier adoption of these targets while QCOM's centers on its own corporate-wide goals.

sentences.text: By fiscal year 2026, we aim to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of NVIDIA's scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions with goal of effecting supplier adoption of science-based targets.

Qualcomm has established near- and long-term science-based emissions reduction targets, which have been approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), including: (1) reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% by 2030 from a 2020 base year; (2) reduce absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by 25% by 2030 from a 2020 base year; and (3) reach net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by 2040.
